title: Witotoan languages - Wikipedia
text: Witotoan (also Huitotoan or Uitotoan, occasionally known as Huitoto-Ocaina to distinguish it from Bora-Witoto) is a small language family of southeastern Colombia (Amazonas Department) and the neighbouring region of Peru.

title: Nüpode Huitoto language - Wikipedia
text: Nüpode Huitoto belongs to the Witotoan language family. Along with Mɨnɨca and Murai, it is one of the three Witoto Proper languages.

title: Witoto Language and the Witoto Indian Tribe (Huitoto, Guitoto, Komine ...
text: Witoto is a Witotoan language of South America, spoken by 4000 people in Columbia and Peru. There are three major varieties of Witoto spoken today-- Murui, Minica and Nipode-- but linguists disagree on whether these are distinct languages or dialects of a single Witoto language.

title: Traversing language barriers: 'Witoto' signal drums from Northwest Amazonia
text: The 'Witoto' people from Northwest Amazonia practised long distance drum communication, used for relaying messages among their villages. The messages were encoded on a pair of hollowed-out wooden drums, and appear to have been 'drummed codes', with only some iconic relation to the sound structure of the spoken language.
